executiveSummary: OT/ICS risk remains elevated this week due to active, multi-actor campaigns against PLCs, exposed HMIs, and edge infrastructure, combined with new and ongoing exploitation of software supply-chain systems and internet-facing appliances. Active, AI-assisted threat activity targeting Siemens S7 PLCs via S7comm (TCP/102) raises direct process-manipulation risk to Water/Wastewater, Energy, and Critical Manufacturing operators. Security Advisory Iranian-affiliated actors continue exploiting internet-exposed PLCs (Rockwell, Schneider, Siemens), modifying logic and disabling alarms with observed operational impacts; immediate removal of direct internet access and logic integrity checks are prioritized. Security Advisory Pro-Russia hacktivists are opportunistically compromising VNC-exposed HMIs in WWS/Energy, changing setpoints and suppressing alarms, causing downtime and loss of view; eliminate VNC exposure and enforce MFA on remote access. Security Advisory MikroTik RouterOS edge devices are under active exploitation with KEV listings; incidents show persistent rogue accounts and flagged devices post-update-assume compromise, patch immediately, and restrict WAN management. Supporting Report CISA KEV JFrog Artifactory exploitation (auth bypass + token abuse) enables admin takeover, malicious plugin deployment, and Rust backdoors-significant software supply-chain risk; patch, rotate tokens, and audit for persistence. View Article EV charging infrastructure and industrial drives present direct OT manipulation pathways: unauthenticated OCPP/WebSocket RCE in EVSE and code/firmware tampering in Danfoss iC7 VFDs warrant immediate segmentation and update planning. CISA Bulletin CISA Bulletin CISA/NSA/FBI advise urgent router-hardening against Russian state-nexus activity abusing SNMP/SMI to siphon configs and pivot-enforce SNMPv3 authPriv, disable SMI, and block risky management ports. items: Pro-Russia hacktivists: opportunistic HMI intrusions via exposed VNC targeting WWS/Energy. Security Advisory
Iran-aligned groups: PLC access/modification with AOI/logic tampering and alarm suppression. Security Advisory
APT using AI-assisted workflows (APT29 overlap) to accelerate malware rebuilds and credential theft against government/defense targets-monitor for polymorphism and DNS hijacking vectors. View Article
Mirage Kitten (Iran-aligned): NodeRabbit/PollCat targeting aviation/FinTech with Cloudflare/Azure C2; strong CI relevance for aerospace supply chains. Vendor Report
Head Mare APT: TrueConf server RCE to weaponize installers (PhantomCore/PhantomGraph) impacting energy/transport orgs in-region; treat conferencing servers as high-value ingress. Vendor Report

relevance: Multiple advisories detail direct, near-term risk to OT controls: Siemens S7 threats and Iranian PLC exploitation target core control logic, while HMI compromise campaigns (VNC) show real-world impact (loss of view, unsafe changes). Concurrently, edge-router exploitation and DevOps repository intrusions increase the likelihood of enterprise-to-OT pivot and supply-chain poisoning. EV charging and industrial drive exposures create sector-specific process manipulation vectors. Net result: a broad, multi-vector risk environment for OT operators requiring immediate exposure reduction, segmentation, and targeted patching/hunting.

items: Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway pre-auth RCE (CVE-2026-8452) with public PoC-critical for perimeter gateways; patch and hunt for web shells/log anomalies. JPCERT/CC
Microsoft Patch Tuesday includes exploited EoP and critical RCEs (DNS, Shell, RRAS/MSMQ)-prioritize ICS-adjacent servers and HMIs in maintenance windows. Krebs SANS ISC
OPC UA stack risks (Eclipse Milo) and other CI-relevant issues aggregated in CISA bulletins-update, enforce SignAndEncrypt, and disable anonymous endpoints. CISA Bulletin
Arrowhead/Ditto IIoT: auth bypass and SSRF enabling remote admin/cloud control-patch and strictly segment management planes. CISA Bulletin

descriptions: Internet-facing exposure: scanning for VNC (5900-5910), PLC ports (102/44818/502/2222), router SNMP/SMI (161/162/4786). (Recon; ATT&CK TA0043)
Initial access: auth bypass on routers/devices; exploitation of gateway/DevOps appliances (NetScaler, Artifactory, GitLab). (T1190)
Privilege escalation & persistence: rogue accounts on routers; application passwords in Zimbra; malicious plugins (Groovy) and backdoors on DevOps servers. (T1136, T1053, T1546)
Lateral movement: VPN/RDP/SMB; misuse of SCCM/AD; SSH tunneling; abuse of cloud tokens. (T1021, T1550, T1557)
Command & control: MQTT/Matrix, DNS/HTTPS exfil, cloud services (OneDrive/Graph, Azure Websites). (T1071, T1095)
Impact on OT: PLC logic writes, alarm suppression, HMI setpoint changes; EVSE and VFD control manipulation. (ICS: T0831 Modify Control Logic; T0829 Manipulate I/O)

outlook72h: Conduct an exposure sweep for VNC/HMI, PLC ports, and router management on internet perimeters; immediately block or proxy with MFA. Emergency MikroTik remediation window: patch, audit, and rotate credentials; monitor for repeat compromise attempts. Initiate Artifactory/GitLab compromise assessments; rotate tokens/keys and validate CI/CD pipelines/artifact signatures. Stage PLC/SCADA logic integrity checks and backup verification; enable ICS protocol monitoring for unauthorized writes. Prioritize patching of NetScaler and Microsoft September updates on OT-adjacent hosts; deploy mitigations where patching must wait.
